nm_frog_prince.blurb: Frog Prince is a compact wall next to the Enchanted Tower, a few steps along a trail from the tower's base. All 19 routes are bolted sport lines, and the grades lean hard: one 5.9, a few 5.10s, then mostly 5.11 and 5.12 with three 5.13s at the top end. The climbing is short, steep and bouldery, so expect power over endurance. The hardest lines sit on the very steep section at the end of the path, while easier routes flank it on either side. Most of the wall stays in shade, though one left-hand 5.10 picks up early sun. It works well as a training stop or a warm-up before the tower.

nm_el_rito_traditional_area.blurb: The traditional area sits in the Carson National Forest above the village of El Rito, further up the drainage than the sport cliffs. It is a single large conglomerate face, around 100 m tall, with routes that run to about 200 feet in two pitches. All 19 routes here are gear-protected and the grades stay gentle: some easy terrain, a cluster in the 5.6 to 5.8 range, and a few at 5.9. The wall is less steep than the cobble-covered sport area, and protection is generally good, which makes it a sensible place for newer trad leaders to build experience. Routes finish on a ridge, so plan the walk-off before you tie in.

nm_mad_cow_wall.blurb: Mad Cow Wall is one of the main cliffs in Last Chance Canyon, in the Lincoln National Forest country north of Carlsbad. It holds 19 bolted sport routes on limestone, ranging from 5.11 to 5.13 with the bulk in the 5.12s. The cliff stretches several hundred yards and faces northeast, running from just past vertical to quite steep. Lines are generally longer than elsewhere in the canyon, and the first few go up steep orange tiers. Because it receives almost no winter sun it can feel cold in the cooler months, so it is mostly a warm-season stop. Strong 5.12 climbers will find the most to do here.

nm_north_wall.blurb: North Wall is a shaded crag in the northern part of The Box near Socorro, tucked on the back side of Red Wall. Sixteen of its 19 routes are sport and three are trad, with grades from 5.8 up to 5.13 and most falling between 5.10 and 5.12. Routes are short and bouldery, usually vertical to a touch overhanging, with a hard start and an easier finish. The rock is rhyolite. Staying in shade most of the day makes it pleasant in spring and fall, cold in winter and warm in midsummer. It suits climbers who like punchy, powerful moves more than long sustained pitches.

nm_fire_wall.blurb: Fire Wall is a west-facing band of cliff in the Upper Level Walls of Comales Canyon, in the mountains south of Taos. Eighteen of its 19 routes are bolted sport lines and one is trad. Grades run from 5.7 to the low 5.12s, with the largest group at 5.11 and a decent handful at 5.9 and 5.10, so it has something for climbers across the middle grades. The wall sits directly above Water Wall and takes the afternoon sun hard because few live trees grow on the bench beneath it, which makes it a better choice for cooler days or mornings that start early.
